## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Add coverage for adopting an already matching setting; the current tests do not protect the change-recording behavior that distinguishes adoption from replacement.

## Changes
The pull request adds an adoption mode that overwrites existing settings and records adopted keys for persistence. It also adds tests for adoption and replacement with differing values.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — tests — Test adoption of an already matching setting — For an existing `{"theme":"dark"}` and identical incoming settings with `adopt=True`, no test checks that adoption still records the key and persists the configuration. Your adoption test only covers differing values. — A regression that silently skips matching adopted keys would pass every current test. — Fix: Extend `test_adopt_updates_setting` with a matching-value case covering the returned changes and persisted bytes.
